items.followUp: Explain why viruses are considered to lie at the boundary between living and non-living things.

rubric.why: Identifies their exclusion from cellular classification.
rubric.description: Viruses lack cellular organization and are not placed in the five-kingdom classification.
rubric.how: Award for stating both their acellular nature and their exclusion from the five kingdoms.

rubric.why: Describes a non-living characteristic of viruses.
rubric.description: Outside a living host, viruses are inert and can be crystallized.
rubric.how: Award for the inactive or crystallized state outside a host.

rubric.why: Describes a living characteristic of viruses.
rubric.description: Inside a living host cell, viruses replicate using the host's machinery.
rubric.how: Award for replication in a host cell.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic viral components relevant to their status.
rubric.description: A virus contains DNA or RNA enclosed in a protein coat.
rubric.how: Award for identifying genetic material and its protein covering.

modelAnswer: Viruses are acellular; they have no cytoplasm, nucleus or other cellular organization, so they are not placed in the five-kingdom classification.
Outside a living host cell, a virus is inactive and may be crystallized, showing a non-living characteristic.
Inside a suitable host cell, it uses the host's machinery to replicate, showing a living characteristic.
A virus consists of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat; therefore, viruses are regarded as being at the boundary between living and non-living things.

items.followUp: List the main products of the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and state how each is formed.

rubric.why: Recognizes the capture of light energy that starts the reactions.
rubric.description: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy.
rubric.how: Award for naming chlorophyll or photosystems and the absorption of light.

rubric.why: Identifies the source of electrons and hydrogen ions.
rubric.description: Light energy splits water into electrons, hydrogen ions and oxygen.
rubric.how: Award for stating that water is split by light.

rubric.why: Identifies ATP formation in the light reactions.
rubric.description: Electron transport drives ATP formation by photophosphorylation.
rubric.how: Award for linking ATP production with photophosphorylation or electron transport.

rubric.why: Identifies the reduced electron carrier produced.
rubric.description: NADP accepts electrons and hydrogen to form NADPH.
rubric.how: Award for stating that NADP is reduced to NADPH.

rubric.why: Identifies oxygen as a product of water splitting.
rubric.description: Oxygen is released as a by-product of photolysis.
rubric.how: Award for naming oxygen and indicating that it is released.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy in the photosystems.
Light energy splits water molecules into electrons, hydrogen ions and oxygen; this process is called photolysis.
Electrons pass along an electron transport chain, and their energy is used to form ATP by photophosphorylation.
NADP accepts electrons and hydrogen ions and is reduced to NADPH.
Oxygen is released as a by-product; ATP and NADPH are used in the light-independent reactions.

items.followUp: Compare simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion, giving one example of a substance transported by each.

rubric.why: States the shared direction of passive movement.
rubric.description: Both processes move substances down their concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award for indicating movement from higher to lower concentration for both.

rubric.why: Distinguishes simple diffusion by its route across the membrane.
rubric.description: Simple diffusion occurs directly through the membrane without a transport protein.
rubric.how: Award for describing direct passage through the lipid bilayer or absence of a transport protein.

rubric.why: Distinguishes facilitated diffusion by its membrane transport proteins.
rubric.description: Facilitated diffusion uses specific channel or carrier proteins.
rubric.how: Award for naming a channel or carrier protein.

rubric.why: Identifies both as passive transport.
rubric.description: Neither process requires cellular energy (ATP).
rubric.how: Award for stating that both occur without ATP.

modelAnswer: Both diffusion and facilitated diffusion are passive processes: substances move from higher to lower concentration without using ATP.
In simple diffusion, small molecules pass directly through the cell membrane's lipid bilayer, without a transport protein.
In facilitated diffusion, a substance crosses the membrane down its concentration gradient through a specific channel or carrier protein.
Thus, the main difference is that facilitated diffusion requires a membrane protein, whereas simple diffusion does not.

items.followUp: Compare the energy released by the oxidation of one gram of carbohydrates, proteins and lipids.

rubric.why: Gives the energy yield of lipids and identifies their high energy value.
rubric.description: Lipids yield about 9 kcal per gram, the greatest energy yield among these food groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the value and 1 mark for identifying lipids as the highest-yielding.

rubric.why: Gives the energy yield of proteins.
rubric.description: Proteins yield about 4 kcal per gram.
rubric.how: Award for the correct approximate value.

rubric.why: Provides the comparison needed to interpret the claim.
rubric.description: Carbohydrates also yield about 4 kcal per gram.
rubric.how: Award for the correct approximate value.

rubric.why: Clarifies the role of proteins rather than treating them as the body's preferred fuel.
rubric.description: Proteins are mainly used for growth and repair; they can provide energy, but are not normally the preferred energy source.
rubric.how: Award for stating the main structural role or that proteins are not the preferred fuel.

modelAnswer: When food molecules are oxidized in cells, their chemical energy is released.
One gram of lipid yields about 9 kcal, while one gram of protein yields about 4 kcal.
One gram of carbohydrate also yields about 4 kcal.
Therefore, lipids are the most concentrated energy source per gram; the statement is not fully correct if it calls proteins the best energy source as well.
Proteins can be used for energy, but their main roles are growth and repair, and they are not normally the body's preferred fuel.

items.followUp: Draw a labeled diagram showing how biology combines with chemistry, physics and mathematics to form interdisciplinary sciences.

rubric.why: Checks that the diagram identifies biology as the central subject.
rubric.description: Biology is clearly shown as the central subject.
rubric.how: Award for a central Biology label.

rubric.why: Checks for correct labels of interdisciplinary sciences.
rubric.description: The diagram correctly labels combinations such as biochemistry and biophysics (and may include other valid examples).
rubric.how: Award for at least two correctly named interdisciplinary sciences.

modelAnswer: Write “Biology” in a central circle.
Draw lines from it to surrounding labels: “Chemistry — Biochemistry,” “Physics — Biophysics,” “Mathematics — Biomathematics,” and “Geography — Biogeography.”
Label the connections clearly; no particular measurements are required.

items.followUp: What do the Greek words “bios” and “logos” mean?

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of the first Greek word.
rubric.description: Bios means life.
rubric.how: Award for giving the meaning of bios.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of the second Greek word.
rubric.description: Logos means study or knowledge.
rubric.how: Award for giving the meaning of logos.

modelAnswer: Biology is derived from the Greek words “bios” and “logos.”
“Bios” means life.
“Logos” means study or knowledge.

items.followUp: Define biostatistics and state how it is used in biology.

rubric.why: Identifies the mathematical basis of biometry.
rubric.description: Biometry applies mathematical methods to biology.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning the application of mathematics or statistical methods.

rubric.why: Specifies the biological subject matter to which those methods are applied.
rubric.description: The methods are used to measure, analyze or interpret biological data or phenomena.
rubric.how: Award for linking the methods to biological data, problems or phenomena.

modelAnswer: Biometry is the application of mathematical and statistical methods to biological problems.
It is used to measure and analyze biological data and phenomena.

items.followUp: Name the organism that causes malaria and the mosquito that transmits it to humans.

rubric.why: Identifies the mosquito involved in transmission.
rubric.description: The female Anopheles mosquito is associated with humans as a blood-feeding parasite and malaria vector.
rubric.how: Award for identifying Anopheles, preferably the female mosquito.

rubric.why: Identifies the parasite transmitted in this association.
rubric.description: The mosquito can transmit Plasmodium, the malaria parasite, to humans.
rubric.how: Award for naming Plasmodium or clearly identifying the malaria parasite.

modelAnswer: The female Anopheles mosquito feeds on human blood and acts as a vector of malaria.
It can transmit the Plasmodium parasite to humans through its bite.
